problems.title: Ambient light is not integrated through each learned code
problems.source_location: Section 3.1, PDF p.4, Eqs.(5)–(6); network.py, lines 131–178
claim: Equations (5)–(6) require ambient contribution proportional to \(I_{\rm amb}\int D_i(t)\,dt\). `network.py` instead adds a shared factor based on \(500\) to every \(1000\)-sample channel.
analysis: Independent normalization does not force equal code sums. For valid code sums \((250,750,500,200)\) and ambient scale \(0.6\), the coded contributions are \((150,450,300,120)\); the shared implementation gives \((300,300,300,300)\). Half-duty channels are a passing special case.
result: The public forward model imposes an unenforced equal-duty assumption. Its historical measurement effect is unknown.
assumptions: Only the cited paper version and explicitly described mathematical or implementation conditions are assessed.
repair: Use the actual per-channel code sum, including sample spacing and accumulation factors, in both expected intensities and information-loss curves. Derive noise variance from those same corrected means.
problems.impact_rationale: This is a release forward-model discrepancy; experimental damage has not been quantified.
problems.existing_correction_status: An explicit local correction is described; author adoption and a corresponding published erratum are not established.

problems.title: The information expression is not the stated Fisher information
problems.source_location: Section 3.3, PDF p.6, Eq.(9); loss_function.py, lines 6–23; train.py, line 186
claim: For Gaussian measurements with mean \(\mu(d)\) and variance \(V(d)=\mu(d)+\nu\), Eq.(9) requires \(J=\mu^{\prime2}/V+V^{\prime2}/(2V^2)\). `loss_function.py` introduces a second-derivative term and different coefficients.
analysis: Taking the expectation of the squared Gaussian score yields the displayed nonnegative Fisher expression. A second derivative of the mean does not appear in that identity. A finite positive-variance quadratic mean can make the implemented sum negative while Eq.(9)’s finite-difference sum is positive, so the discrepancy is not a common normalization. Such a quadratic is a diagnostic mean, not an asserted learned code curve.
result: The routine does not compute Eq.(9). This does not prove an observed optimization failure in the paper.
assumptions: Only the cited paper version and explicitly described mathematical or implementation conditions are assessed.
repair: Use \([1/V+1/(2V^2)](g\mu)^2\) under the same mean-dependent variance model. State finite-difference boundaries, the depth/phase Jacobian and the design distribution used for accumulation.
problems.impact_rationale: The expression is wrong at a local implementation interface; original training and performance consequences remain uncertain.
problems.existing_correction_status: An explicit local correction is described; author adoption and a corresponding published erratum are not established.
